name: Kerberos Clock Skew Fixes (faketime / ntpdate)
description: Fixes 'KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW (Clock skew too great)' errors when running Kerberos tooling (impacket, certipy, Rubeus, evil-winrm with -k) from Linux against a DC whose clock differs from yours by more than 5 minutes. Either sync the host clock or wrap a single command with faketime so only that process sees the DC's time.
source: HTB Fluffy engagement; common AD-from-Linux gotcha
notes:
=== THE ERROR ===
  Kerberos SessionError: KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW(Clock skew too great)
Kerberos rejects tickets when the client and KDC clocks differ by more than the
allowed skew (default 5 minutes). AD labs and HTB boxes often run a different time
than your attack host.

=== OPTION A - SYNC THE WHOLE HOST (simplest, but changes your clock) ===
  sudo timedatectl set-ntp off        # stop NTP from re-correcting
  sudo ntpdate <dc_ip>                 # set host clock to the DC
  # or: sudo rdate -n <dc_ip>
  # when done, re-enable normal time: sudo timedatectl set-ntp on

=== OPTION B - faketime (does NOT touch your real clock) ===
  faketime "$(ntpdate -q <dc_ip> | cut -d ' ' -f 1,2)" impacket-getST ...
  # only the wrapped command sees the DC's time; the rest of your system is unaffected.
  # preferred when other tools/logging depend on your real clock.

=== OPTION C - per-tool time ===
  Some tools accept an explicit time or auto-handle skew; when in doubt, use faketime.

=== WHY IT MATTERS IN A CHAIN ===
  PKINIT (Shadow Credentials, ESC1/ESC16 cert auth) and getST/getTGT all fail on skew.
  Fix skew FIRST, before shadow creds, ADCS, or getST, or you will chase phantom errors.

examples.label: Sync host clock to the DC
examples.command: sudo timedatectl set-ntp off && sudo ntpdate 10.129.65.243

examples.label: Wrap a single certipy run with faketime (no host clock change)
examples.command: faketime "$(ntpdate -q 10.129.65.243 | cut -d ' ' -f 1,2)" certipy-ad shadow auto -u user@fluffy.htb -p pass -account winrm_svc -dc-ip 10.129.65.243

recommended.note: PKINIT in shadow creds fails on skew - fix time first.

explain:
Wraps any Kerberos command so it runs with the DC's clock, curing 'KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW (Clock skew too great)' from Linux without changing your system time:
  ntpdate -q <dc_ip>        query (do not set) the DC's current time
  cut -d ' ' -f 1,2         take the date and time fields from that output
  faketime "..." <kerberos_command>   run impacket/certipy/Rubeus/evil-winrm -k with that faked clock
The wrapped tool sees a time within 5 minutes of the DC, so PKINIT/AS-REQ succeeds.
